title: From Literature to ‘ReWA’: Discussing Reproductive Well-being in HCI
reasoning: The paper extensively evaluates the intersection of reproductive health technologies with religious beliefs, particularly Islamic values, and cultural norms. It analyzes how religious practices (e.g., prayer, fasting) and modesty standards (e.g., purdah, haya) impact the design and use of digital tools. Religious knowledge systems are integrated as a core orientation within the proposed ReWA framework, and the paper reviews a substantial body of literature (e.g., references 1, 2, 33, 54-56, 92, 93, 134) specifically focused on religious and ethical dimensions in HCI.
